findings.title: Potential URL normalization bypass due to removed double-slash handling
findings.description: Removing leading double slashes (`//`) from URLs can lead to path traversal or URL parsing vulnerabilities in specific contexts (e.g., SSRF or open redirect). For example, an attacker-controlled URL like `http://127.0.0.1:10000//../` might be intended to resolve to a different path or bypass restrictions, but the modification to single `/` changes the path semantics. The diff *removes* this sanitization, meaning the original code was trying to normalize paths that start with `//` to `/`. By removing this normalization, the library now passes `//...` to urllib3. Depending on how the underlying HTTP stack (urllib3/http.client) handles double slashes, this could potentially be abused to bypass host/path validation or cause unexpected behavior, especially in proxied requests or when dealing with `//` in authority/path components.
findings.suggestion: Investigate if passing `//` paths to urllib3 introduces any bypass of URL normalization checks. Ensure that the underlying HTTP library correctly treats `//` in the path component as a path segment, not as an authority separator. If the removal is intentional for RFC 3986 compliance, ensure that upstream validation (e.g., `urldefragauth` or proxy logic) handles these edge cases securely without allowing SSRF or host confusion.
